A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MMEarth-Bench and TTT-MMR. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and added analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original finetuning, linear-probing and test-time-training results across five environmental tasks and two test splits in Section 5 and the supplementary material.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds evaluated models, a modality ablation, long-tail analysis and quantitative reconstruction results.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains joint training, normalized per-modality gradient updates, frozen reconstruction decoders, encoder resets and geographic batching. The additional model variants serve as experimental comparators; the proposed TTT-MMR procedure is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same biomass, soil nitrogen, soil organic carbon, soil pH and species datasets, with the same 12 modalities and geographic coverage. The new analyses examine the existing data rather than introduce another task or test environment.

E2.justification: v2 adds Galileo and randomly initialized ConvNeXtV2A-MM to finetuning, linear-probing and JT/TTT comparisons. Galileo S2 also enters the input-modality comparisons. These additions substantially strengthen the comparator set, particularly through the multimodal model trained from scratch; v1's randomly initialized baseline accepted only RGB.

E3.justification: Added diagnostic protocols stratify residuals and species average precision by frequency, omit individual reconstruction modalities, and evaluate reconstruction using R² or categorical accuracy. The original splits, training subsets, 100-epoch budget, batch size and validation-based selection remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds long-tail analysis (Figure 8), a DINOv3 Sat leave-one-modality-out ablation (Figure A.16), an analysis of selected best models (Table A.17), and quantitative reconstruction diagnostics (Tables A.18–A.27). These substantially extend v1's linear-probing comparisons, relative-improvement analysis and qualitative reconstruction visualization.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly reports using one seed for the new long-tail analysis and modality ablation. The original benchmark retains seeds 41–43, standard-error reporting and one-sided Wilcoxon tests with Holm-Bonferroni correction; no increase in its repeated-run count is reported.

E6.justification: The original raw finetuning, linear-probing and JT/TTT scores are retained, but substantial results are added. ConvNeXtV2A-MM ranks first overall on the random split and fourth geographically with full training data (Table A.10). Table A.15 adds negative random-split TTT relative improvements for some new-model configurations. New diagnostic findings are reported, and the expanded Figure 7 comparison reports p < 0.05 rather than v1's p < 0.01.

T1.justification: The reconstruction-loss and normalized-gradient update mathematics remain equivalent despite revised notation and equation formatting. Metric definitions and geographic encodings are retained; neither version adds substantive theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion newly emphasize that multimodal training from scratch can compete with pretraining given sufficient labels, and that geographic batching particularly benefits rare samples. These substantially broaden the paper's principal conclusions beyond v1's benchmark and aggregate adaptation findings.

C2.justification: v2 expands interpretation of multimodal inputs versus pretraining, proposes gradient alignment and reduced dilution as explanations for long-tail gains, and interprets the ablation as evidence against dependence on one modality. Table A.15 also explicitly qualifies TTT's benefits by discussing deterioration for Galileo and ConvNeXtV2A-MM on the random split.

D1.justification: v2 documents Galileo's configuration and ConvNeXtV2A-MM's categorical encoding, spatial broadcasting and 926 input channels. Table A.16 newly reports selected TTT iteration averages, and Explorer split filtering changes from planned to reported as implemented. Table A.9 restates existing hyperparameters rather than changing them.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hong et al.'s foundation-model survey and expands positioning relative to weak-label and auxiliary-task TTA. Galileo was already cited in v1 but receives fuller discussion in v2. The broader related-work framework remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 edits the abstract, introduction and results, consolidates v1 Sections 5.2–5.5 under one Results subsection, and moves the existing hyperparameter discussion into the appendix. Most related-work, dataset, method and data-construction prose remains closely matched.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one, rearranges Figure 1 and Table 3, and expands model legends and table columns. New analysis figures and diagnostic tables substantially change the visual presentation. The enlarged duplicate figures from v1's Section S.6 are removed while their underlying plots remain.

improvement.justification: The multimodal baseline trained from scratch addresses an important missing control in v1's assessment of pretraining. The modality ablation and quantitative reconstruction diagnostics also substantially strengthen scrutiny of TTT. Some conclusions remain limited by single-seed evidence, and Table A.17 names MPMAE as the best geographic-biomass model although Table A.10 ranks ConvNeXtV2A-MM first. These weaknesses temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial improvement in the paper's empirical foundation.
